overview: Tunisia is the northernmost country in Africa, on the Mediterranean coast. Its capital and largest city is Tunis. In ancient times it was home to Carthage, the great rival of Rome. Tunisia became independent from France in 1956, and its revolution in 2011 sparked the protests known as the Arab Spring. Arabic is the official language.

geography.text: The north of Tunisia is hilly and green, at the eastern end of the Atlas Mountains. The centre has dry plains and large salt lakes such as Chott el Djerid, and the south is part of the Sahara. Its long Mediterranean coastline includes the island of Djerba.

history.text: Phoenicians founded Carthage near today's Tunis, and it fought Rome in the Punic Wars until it was destroyed in 146 BC. Arab armies brought Islam in the 600s, and Kairouan became a holy city. France ruled Tunisia from 1881 until independence in 1956. In 2010–11 Tunisia's revolution began the Arab Spring.

events.title: Hannibal
events.text: Hannibal crosses the Alps with elephants to attack Rome.

events.title: Revolution
events.text: Protests remove President Ben Ali and spark the Arab Spring.

government.text: Tunisia began the Arab Spring in 2011 and became a democracy. Since 2021 President Kais Saied has suspended parliament, rewritten the constitution and greatly increased his own powers, and critics have been jailed.

economy.text: Tunisia exports olive oil, clothing, phosphates and car parts, and tourism is important. It is one of the world's largest olive oil producers.

culture.text: Tunisia's history stretches from Carthage to Roman and Islamic cities such as Kairouan. The Star Wars films were partly shot in its desert, and the set of Luke Skywalker's home in Matmata is a hotel. Harissa, a hot chilli paste, is listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Carthage
items.text: Ruins of the ancient city near Tunis.

items.title: El Djem
items.text: One of the largest Roman amphitheatres.

items.title: Harissa
items.text: Chilli paste listed by UNESCO in 2022.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and Tunisia won the Africa Cup of Nations in 2004. Ons Jabeur became the first Arab woman to reach a Grand Slam final, and swimmer Ahmed Hafnaoui won Olympic gold in 2021.

didYouKnow: Parts of Star Wars were filmed in Tunisia, and a desert town gave its name to Luke Skywalker's home planet, Tatooine.
Tunisia's revolution in 2011 began the Arab Spring.
